content.introduction: The Financial Aid Office helps students understand and access funding options including scholarships, grants, loans, and work-study programs.

sections.title: Types of Aid
sections.content:
Grants (Free Money):
- Pell Grant: Federal need-based (up to $7,395)
- SEOG: Supplemental federal grant
- State grants: Varies by state
- University grants: Institutional aid

Scholarships (Free Money):
- Merit-based awards
- Department scholarships
- External scholarships

Loans (Must Repay):
- Direct Subsidized: Need-based, no interest while enrolled
- Direct Unsubsidized: Available regardless of need
- Parent PLUS: Parents borrow for student

Work-Study:
- Part-time campus employment
- Earn money for expenses

sections.title: Applying for Aid
sections.content:
FAFSA:
- Required for all federal aid
- Opens October 1 each year
- Priority deadline: March 1
- Use IRS Data Retrieval Tool

Scholarship Applications:
- University scholarships: March 1 deadline
- Department scholarships: Contact your major
- External scholarships: Various deadlines

sections.title: Understanding Your Award
sections.content:
Award Letter:
- Lists all aid offered
- Shows Cost of Attendance
- Indicates Expected Family Contribution

Accepting Aid:
- Log into student portal
- Accept, reduce, or decline each award
- Only borrow what you need

sections.title: Maintaining Eligibility
sections.content:
Satisfactory Academic Progress:
- Minimum 2.0 GPA
- Complete 67% of attempted credits
- Finish within 150% of program length

Enrollment Requirements:
- Full-time: 12+ credits
- Half-time: 6-11 credits (minimum for loans)

sections.title: Contact Us
sections.content:
Location: Administration Building, Room 200
Phone: (555) 123-4540
Email: finaid@university.edu

Hours:
Monday-Friday: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM
Walk-in hours: 10 AM - 3 PM
Appointments recommended for complex questions

content.conclusion: Apply for aid early! Many programs have limited funding and are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.

content.introduction: The Student Accounts office (Bursar) handles tuition billing, payments, refunds, and payment plans.

sections.title: Viewing Your Bill
sections.content:
Access Your Account:
1. Log into the student portal
2. Navigate to Student Finances
3. View current balance and charges

Bill Components:
- Tuition and fees
- Housing and meal plan
- Health insurance (if applicable)
- Course fees
- Less: Financial aid applied

sections.title: Payment Options
sections.content:
How to Pay:
- Online via student portal (ACH or card)
- By mail (check or money order)
- In person at Bursar's Office
- Wire transfer (international)

Payment Methods:
- E-check (no fee)
- Credit/debit card (2.75% fee)
- 529 plan disbursements
- Third-party billing

sections.title: Payment Plans
sections.content:
Monthly Payment Plan:
- Spread payments over the semester
- $50 enrollment fee per semester
- Auto-debit from bank account
- Enroll by payment deadline

How to Enroll:
1. Go to Student Accounts in portal
2. Select Payment Plan
3. Choose number of installments
4. Set up auto-pay

sections.title: Refunds
sections.content:
Financial Aid Refunds:
- Disbursed after aid exceeds charges
- Direct deposit (fastest - 3-5 days)
- Paper check (7-10 days)

Withdrawal Refunds:
- Based on withdrawal date
- See refund schedule in academic calendar
- Housing refunds have separate policy

sections.title: Important Deadlines
sections.content:
Fall Semester: August 1
Spring Semester: January 1
Summer: May 1

Late Fees:
- 1.5% monthly on unpaid balance
- Registration hold for past due accounts
- No transcripts until balance paid

content.conclusion: Set up direct deposit for faster refunds. Contact us before the due date if you're having trouble paying.

content.introduction: The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is required for all federal financial aid including grants, loans, and work-study.

sections.title: Before You Begin
sections.content:
Documents Needed:
- Social Security Number
- Driver's license (if applicable)
- Federal tax returns (yours and parents')
- W-2 forms and income records
- Bank statements
- Investment records
- FSA ID (create at studentaid.gov)

Note: Both student and one parent need FSA IDs for dependent students.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Process
sections.content:
1. Create FSA ID
   - Need email and SSN
   - Parents need separate ID

2. Start FAFSA
   - Select correct academic year
   - Enter personal information

3. Answer Dependency Questions
   - Most undergrads are dependent
   - Answer honestly

4. Report Financial Information
   - Use IRS Data Retrieval Tool
   - Report accurately

5. List Schools
   - Add our school code
   - Can list up to 10 schools

6. Sign and Submit
   - Both student and parent sign
   - Use FSA IDs

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
Avoid These Errors:
- Wrong Social Security Number
- Incorrect income reporting
- Forgetting to sign
- Missing the deadline
- Not listing all schools
- Leaving questions blank
- Using wrong tax year

sections.title: Important Deadlines
sections.content:
Federal Deadline: June 30
State Deadline: Varies (often earlier)
University Priority: March 1

Tip: Apply as early as possible after October 1. Some aid is first-come, first-served.

sections.title: After Submission
sections.content:
Next Steps:
1. Review Student Aid Report (SAR)
2. Check for errors and correct
3. Note Expected Family Contribution
4. Wait for award letters from schools
5. Compare offers
6. Accept/decline aid in portal
7. Complete loan counseling if borrowing

content.conclusion: Need help? The Financial Aid Office offers FAFSA completion workshops and one-on-one assistance.
